scope: candidate SQL read-only adapter and fixture
correctedBeforeCi: Explicitly zero each transferred plaintext chunk after the awaited consumer write, including error, cancellation and iterator return.

limits: Milestone 7.3 remains incomplete; this checkpoint only qualifies the candidate operator-export APIs.
Conversation ZIP and browser download are not yet adapted to video streaming (7.3b).
Durable deletion, account closure and capacity release remain for 7.3c.
Inventory, capture, restore, old-format compatibility and migration promotion remain for 7.3d.
Rollback compatibility must be qualified before activation in 7.6.
No actual codec/video decoding, physical phone, hosted throughput or peak process memory measurement is claimed.
A source that ignores AbortSignal and never settles is still awaited; cancellation does not pretend to end outstanding I/O.
Plaintext partial exports may remain in the private output directory after failure; no completion marker is published by the demonstrated caller.
nextAction: 7.3b — ZIP de conversation en flux, sur la même branche ; PR en brouillon jusqu’à 7.6.

jobs.name: MariaDB 11.4

catalogue.name: real MariaDB dormant video catalog reserves, commits and reconciles durable capacity

subtests.name: offline initialization is explicit, idempotent and bound to root and both quotas
candidate DDL rejects weakened checks, keys, ownership links and dirty history
SQL itself enforces encrypted-byte accounting, state, role, digest and ownership
a corrupted durable counter fails every mutation without weakening SQL limits
reserve, commit and release are exact retries, and committed objects cannot be released
current SQL owner, role, session, access and creator gates cannot be bypassed
cleanup after revocation is bound to the original reservation and never authorizes a read
exact owner and global quotas serialize simultaneous reservations without oversubscription
lost acknowledgements after actual reserve and commit transactions survive store recreation
real SQL service and encrypted storage preserve a committed video after a lost acknowledgement

messages.name: real HTTP/SQL video messages are atomic, idempotent, private and visible only through live deliveries

subtests.name: real HTTP captions, concurrent exact retries, history, events and recipient-device notifications agree
delivery GET/HEAD use live SQL authorization, private headers and authenticated Range bytes
HTTP mutations enforce real origin, CSRF, strict shape and committed-owner eligibility
link, event and real notification failures roll back the complete publication without discarding the original
a lost acknowledgement after the native publication COMMIT survives reconstruction without duplicate jobs
the native composite link refuses another conversation and schema inspection refuses weakened foreign keys
video galleries are scoped keyset pages and preserve full unsigned sequence values
persisted revocation, expiration and blocking deny viewing and retries while assigned administrator history survives
a revocation committed during a native send lock wait prevents every publication row
tombstones revoke delivery bytes and old event payloads without resurrecting content or removing another live delivery

videoData.name: real read-only MariaDB client video exports stream authenticated files without changing SQL or source capacity

subtests.name: candidate video reader shares the native read-only snapshot and never returns another client's library
version two export deduplicates original streams, keeps captions and tombstones, and excludes foreign or undelivered originals
the second client gets its own library and shared delivery without the first client's videos or captions
interrupted streams and an unauthentic second block leave no completion marker or source mutation
a lost acknowledgement after the real read-only COMMIT cannot publish COMPLETE and a fresh export still succeeds
